text:
Diego Morales: morning team — hitting weirdness: `kubectl config current-context` returns redwood-prod even though onboarding said redwood-staging. I ran `./onboard.sh --env staging` and it claimed success. Anyone seen this? @Priya (infra)
Priya (infra): congrats Diego. First check: do you have multiple kubeconfig files? `echo $KUBECONFIG` or `ls ~/.kube/*.conf` — our onboarding script writes ~/.kube/redwood-staging and then some folks end up with KUBECONFIG set in their shell rc so you can have a list.
Diego Morales: `echo $KUBECONFIG` outputs `/Users/diego/.kube/config:/Users/diego/.kube/work-kube` — hmm. I thought multiple files merge. How does kubectl decide current-context then?
Sam (devex): short answer: when KUBECONFIG is a list, kubectl merges them but values from later files override earlier ones for map keys; however current-context is taken from the last file in the list that defines it. So ordering matters. You probably have redwood-prod in ~/.kube/config or work-kube that comes after the staging file.
Diego Morales: oh that explains it. Is there an easy way to see which file set the current-context?
Priya (infra): yes: `kubectl config view --raw --minify` will show the raw config used for the current context. Another quick test: `KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/redwood-staging kubectl config current-context` — that runs kubectl against only the staging file.
Diego Morales: tried `KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/redwood-staging kubectl get ns` and it shows team-staging. Cool. What's best practice? should onboarding modify my global config?
Sam (devex): we intentionally don't overwrite users' global configs. Best practices: either 1) export KUBECONFIG with staging first so it takes precedence: `export KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/redwood-staging:~/.kube/config` or 2) use our tiny wrapper function we include in the dotfiles: `kr() { KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/redwood-staging kubectl "$@"; }` so you can run `kr get pods`.
Diego Morales: nice. I'll add the wrapper. One more: when I `kubectl -n team-staging get secrets` I get "Error from server (Forbidden): secrets is forbidden: User \"diego@company\" cannot list resource \"secrets\" in API group \"\" in the namespace \"team-staging\"". I expected read access to configmaps but not secrets. How to request?
Priya (infra): secrets are intentionally restricted. Please file a ticket in #support with the RBAC tag using the template: team, username, namespace, resources needed, reason. For temporary debugging we can grant a short-lived role for up to 4 hours; ping me or @sre-oncall for fast approval.
Diego Morales: great — filing the ticket now. Thanks!
Sam (devex): I'll add a new note to the onboarding doc explaining KUBECONFIG ordering and include the kr wrapper snippet.
Devex Bot: :memo: docs/new-hires/kube.md updated by Sam (devex)
Diego Morales: thanks all! saved my morning :coffee:
